scope: Full Wan unscrew and rinse generation with appearance-difference fallback masks
summary: Both 240-frame generations completed, but dense review found pervasive black block artifacts that reproduce the high-frequency fallback-mask topology. The candidates are rejected despite valid geometry and successful execution; a smooth pose-capsule support route supersedes the mask construction for the next run.
evidence: The immutable runs full-v2/unscrew-bottle-cap/20260811T105115Z-36b79ab0 and full-v2/rinse-bottle/20260811T105114Z-8696b0c3 both decode to 880x512, 240 frames, and 24 FPS.
Every-fourth-frame contact sheets and full-resolution key frames show dense black strokes across the upper background and interaction region in both candidates.

The artifacts align spatially with the fragmented white/black regions in the threshold-64, dilation-3 appearance-difference masks; the clean native place preprocessing instead uses large smooth support regions.
lessons: A nonempty binary mask is not sufficient: high-frequency topology can leak as visible black conditioning artifacts even when mean support coverage looks reasonable.
Fallback masks should be derived from smooth kinematic capsules and object support, with small-component removal, rather than raw scene-difference texture.
limitations: No quality or task claim is made for either rejected candidate.
The diagnosis is based on controlled visual correspondence, not an internal Wan attention trace.
next_actions: Regenerate both tasks using smooth pose-capsule plus blue-object support and retain the same model, seed, prompt, and no-blur settings.
